newsitem.title: USA: San Onofre confirms restart delay at Calif. nuke.
newsitem.headline: San Onofre confirms restart delay at Calif. nuke.

text.p: Officials at the 1,080 megawatt San Onofre 3 nuclear unit confirmed earlier reports that its restart would be delayed until July, Southern California Edison said Thursday in a statement.
The company said the unit would likely return to service around July 10, which is about two weeks later than previously expected.
The Nuclear Regulatory Commission said in Thursday's plant status report that the unit was expected to restart July 6.

The restart was delayed when it was discovered that one of the 91 control assemblies, which regulate the operation and shutdown of the reactor's core, was not withdrawing properly from the reactor core.
The unit, in San Clemente, Calif., has been shut for refueling and repairs since April 12.

The San Onofre plant is 75 percent owned by Southern California Edison, the principal operating unit of Edison International, 20 percent owned by Enova Corp and the remainder owned by local municipalities.
